prompt_text: AI to draft donor thank you letters
response_text:
Here’s a practical overview of how to use AI to draft strong donor thank‑you letters, plus concrete prompts and tools you can start with right away.

---

## 1. What AI is good for in donor thank‑you letters

AI can help you:

- Draft first versions quickly (no more staring at a blank page).
- Maintain consistent quality and tone across your acknowledgments.
- Personalize at scale (referencing specific gifts, programs, and donor history).
- Systematize stewardship (e.g., tiers of letters based on gift size or type).

You still need a human to:
- Check accuracy (gift amount, designation, names).
- Ensure the tone matches your brand.
- Add any sensitive, high‑touch notes for major donors.

---

## 2. A reusable “master prompt” you can paste into any AI tool

Copy/paste this into ChatGPT, Gemini, Poe, etc., then fill in the brackets:

> You are a donor stewardship specialist for **[Organization Name]**, a **[type of org]** that **[1–2 sentence mission]**.  
>   
> Write a **[short/medium/long]**, warm, specific, donor thank‑you letter.  
>   
> **Donor details:**  
> - Name: **[Donor name and how they prefer to be addressed]**  
> - Gift amount: **[amount]**  
> - Gift type: **[one‑time / recurring / event / in‑honor / in‑memory / pledge payment]**  
> - Designation: **[fund/program/campaign name]**  
> - Gift date: **[date]** (you can reference “this week” or “recently” instead of the date)  
> - Donor history: **[first‑time donor / second‑year donor / has given annually since 20XX / total lifetime giving if relevant]**  
> - Notes about donor interests or connection: **[e.g., loves arts education, alum, parent, volunteer, etc.]**  
>   
> **Organization context (use this for impact language; don’t invent facts):**  
> - Our mission: **[mission statement or summary]**  
> - Key programs relevant to this gift: **[2–4 bullets with one‑sentence descriptions each]**  
> - Current impact stats we can reference: **[e.g., “served 1,200 students last year,” “provided 5,000 meals,” etc.]**  
> - Required tax/receipt language (include near the end, in one clear sentence): **[insert your IRS/CRA/legal language]**  
>   
> **Tone and style requirements:**  
> - Tone: **[warm and positive / casual and heartfelt / professional but friendly]**.  
> - Use first person (“I” / “we”) and second person (“you”) often.  
> - Start with an interesting, human opening line, *not* “On behalf of” and not “Dear Friend.”  
> - Show emotion and impact: clearly connect the donor’s gift to what will change for **[beneficiaries]**.  
> - Be concise and conversational, not formal or lofty.  
> - Avoid generic jargon like “we are deeply grateful for your continued support.”  
> - Use contractions (“we’re,” “you’ll”) and a few exclamation marks if they feel natural, but don’t overdo it.  
> - Do **not** ask the donor for anything else in this letter (no new appeals or calls to action).  
>   
> **Sign‑off details:**  
> - Closing should feel personal and warm.  
> - Sign it from: **[Name, Title, Organization]**  
> - Include phone number (and email if appropriate): **[xxx‑xxx‑xxxx, email]**  
>   
> Now, write the letter.

You can save this as a base prompt and tweak only the bracketed fields each time.

---

## 3. Example: Filled‑in prompt + AI‑ready text

Here’s a concrete example you can adapt:

> You are a donor stewardship specialist for Bright Futures Learning Center, a nonprofit that provides free after‑school tutoring and enrichment for low‑income middle school students.  
>   
> Write a medium‑length, warm, specific donor thank‑you letter.  
>   
> Donor details:  
> - Name: Sarah Johnson (address as “Sarah”)  
> - Gift amount: $500  
> - Gift type: one‑time online gift  
> - Designation: “After‑School Tutoring Fund”  
> - Gift date: May 10, 2026  
> - Donor history: second‑year donor; also attended our spring open house last year  
> - Notes: Sarah is particularly interested in supporting girls in STEM.  
>   
> Organization context:  
> - Mission: We help students build confidence and close learning gaps through free tutoring, mentoring, and enrichment programs.  
> - Key programs relevant to this gift:  
>   - After‑School Tutoring: one‑on‑one and small‑group support in math and reading, four days per week.  
>   - STEM Club for Girls: weekly hands‑on projects in coding, robotics, and science.  
> - Impact stats: Last year, we served 180 students; 87% improved at least one grade level in math or reading, and 95% reported feeling more confident at school.  
> - Required language: “No goods or services were provided in exchange for this contribution. Bright Futures Learning Center is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, EIN 12‑3456789.”  
>   
> Tone and style requirements:  
> - Tone: warm and positive, conversational but professional.  
> - Use first person (“I” / “we”) and second person (“you”) often.  
> - Start with a creative, human opening line (not “On behalf of” and not “Dear Friend”).  
> - Show emotion and impact: clearly connect Sarah’s gift to what will change for the students, especially girls in STEM.  
> - Be concise and conversational, not formal or lofty.  
> - Avoid generic jargon like “we are deeply grateful for your continued support.”  
> - Use contractions and a few exclamation marks if they feel natural.  
> - Do not ask Sarah for anything else in this letter.  
>   
> Sign‑off details:  
> - Sign from: Maria Lopez, Executive Director, Bright Futures Learning Center  
> - Include phone and email: 555‑123‑4567, maria@brightfutures.org  
>   
> Now, write the letter.

You can paste something like that into any AI system to get a very usable draft.

---

## 4. Using tiered prompts for automation (by gift size)

If you want to automate via your CRM/Zapier/etc., you can adapt the segmentation framework from result [4]. For example, define four variants of the prompt:

- **Tier 1 (under $250, first‑time)**:  
  - “Write a 150–200 word email… include name, amount, designation, and one concrete impact line.”
- **Tier 2 ($250–$999 or recurring)**:  
  - “Write 250–350 words… reference giving history, one program story, and add required tax language.”
- **Tier 3 ($1,000–$4,999)**:  
  - “Write 350–500 words… reference past interactions and donor interests; draft 2–3 extra sentences for a handwritten note.”
- **Tier 4 ($5,000+)**:  
  - “Write a full, highly personalized letter; also provide bullet‑point phone call talking points and a suggested next stewardship touch.”

Combine these with your CRM data fields (name, amount, program, giving history) and send them to your AI tool via an API.

---

## 5. Tools you can explore (from your search results and beyond)

From the links you shared:

- **Poe “Fundraiser-Thank-You” bot** ([result 1])  
  Pre‑configured for nonprofit thank‑you letters; good if you want a guided experience.

- **Gail Perry Group prompt** ([result 2])  
  Great if you like her “killer thank you letter” style—copy their bolded prompt and fill in your donor info.

- **AI for Education prompt** ([result 3])  
  Tailored to education nonprofits; useful if you’re in that space.

- **Claw Mart article + prompt** ([result 4])  
  Especially helpful if you’re thinking about full automation with webhooks, Zapier, or your CRM.

- **Free‑form generators**:  
  - FreeWill “Thank you notes” tool ([6])  
  - Fundwriter.ai ([8])  
  - Taskade’s donor thank‑you generator ([5])  
  - Bit.ai’s prompt ([9])  
  These are UI‑based tools where you fill a form and get a draft.

You can also just use ChatGPT or Gemini with the master prompt above; you don’t necessarily need a dedicated product unless you want tighter CRM integration.

---

## 6. Safeguards and best practices

When using AI for donor thanks:

1. **Never paste sensitive data.** Omit full addresses, IDs, or anything confidential.
2. **Lock in your brand voice.** Give the AI a short “voice guide” for your org and reuse it.
3. **Human‑review major gifts.** For high‑value donors, treat the AI draft as a starting point only.
4. **Standardize required language.** Always include your exact tax/receipt sentence in the prompt so it’s copied verbatim.
